nodes.title: Revisions
nodes.body: January 19, 1993.  T.D. Philipps; Mote Marine Laboratory

nodes.title: TAXONOMY
nodes.body:
Common Name:  Blacktip shark
Scientific Name: Carcharhinus limbatus

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.body:
Phylum: Chordata
	Class: Elasmobranchiomorphi
	Order: Lamniformes
	Family: Carcharhinidae

Other Common Names:  spot-fin shark (581) small black-tipped shark (52)

nodes.title: VALUE & STATUS
nodes.body:
Commercial:  Marketed fresh or salted, also used for fishmeal (101 791). Various sub-products such as the liver used for oil (791). Skin is also used for leather (101).

Recreational: Often fished for sport (101).

nodes.title: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
nodes.body: Overall:  From Massachusetts to northern Brazil and worldwide in temperate and tropical waters (327 788). Also, northeast Florida through the Gulf of Mexico (101). Reported in the eastern tropical Pacific from Lower California to Peru (52).

nodes.title: By State
nodes.body:
Florida:  Within Study Area: Distributed throughout Florida waters.

Mobility and Migration:

nodes.title: Life Mode
nodes.body: Pelagic, often coming into inshore waters in large schools in association with Spanish mackerel, usually found in offshore and coastal waters frequently in aggregations of 6 or more (788 791). Sometimes seen in schools at the surface (52).

nodes.title: BENTHIC HABITAT
nodes.body:
Habitat Type: Young use shallow beach and bay areas as nursery grounds (860). Frequently the most common shark in clear water cuts and along beaches in Florida and the Bahamas (7881, and one of the commonest pelagic sharks around south Florida (581).

Substrate: No particular substrate is known to be preferred.

nodes.title: REPRODUCTION
nodes.body: Reproductive Mode: Fertilization is internal; reproduction is viviparous (101).

nodes.title: Mating/Spawning
nodes.body:
Males mature at a length of 130-135 cm (4-5 ft) and at an age of 4-5 years (52 101 860). Females mature at a length of 150-155 cm (101 123 860) and at an age of 6-6.8 years (860). In Florida, mating occurs in June and July (860). Gestation period extends from 10 to 12 months (62 101).Young are born in late spring through early summer (101 123). In the Tampa Bay area a 3 to 4 week parturition period extends from late May to early June (860).

Fecundity: Fecundity has been variously reported as 4-6 embryos (101), 1-10 embryos (791), and 3-9 embryos with 4-6 the most common (52).

nodes.title: Length Range
nodes.body:
Juveniles: Size at birth ranges from 48.8 cm to 60 cm (791 860). Smallest neonates in Florida are 62 cm with rapid neonatal growth (860). Growth rates are 25-30 cm by the first annulus; 20 cm/yr during second year; 10 cm/yr through adolescence; 5-7 cm/yr after maturity (860). Branstetter (860) gave the equation from fork length to total length as
[eq]
TL=1.16(FL) + 5.71
[/eq]

Adults: Maximum size reported is 152-198 cm (52 123) although Robins (788) gives the figure of 2.5 m. Largest males in Florida were 8.6 years of age and largest females ranged from 8 to 9.3 years of age (860).

nodes.title: FOOD HABITS
nodes.body: Feeds on small schooling fishes, menhaden, rays, squid, and other schooling fishes (52 62 101 123 791). Remains of crabs have also been found in their stomachs (123). Small blacktips have been found in the stomachs of other sharks (5 2) .
